📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

According to recent reports, england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the massive delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon stated of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Industry observers note that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

Recent findings suggest that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

According to recent reports, czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

It has been revealed that england had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Recent findings suggest that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

Recent findings suggest that “I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold stated later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

Industry observers note that two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

Sources indicate that kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

It has been revealed that “If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel noted when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

Industry observers note that “He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel noted.

Sources indicate that “He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”.

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker explained that the club had attempted to push the Frenchman’s recovery but were struggling to get him ready.

“We tried to push it a bit, but it looks a little bit unlikely and we’ll leave it as long as we can before making a decision,” said the West Ham boss.

Personally, my choice would be to give young Fin Herrick a chance.

I was speaking to my Hammers Chat counterpart Geo during our West Ham v Preston preview this week, and he made an excellent observation.

The one thing Mads Hermansen has consistently been good at is his distribution with the ball at his feet.

Unfortunately, his clanger for Denmark in their last game means even that aspect of his performances is now under scrutiny.

He’s got the yips: West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, whose recent performances have raised concerns about his confidence.

I actually think the best thing we could possibly do for Hermansen would be to give him a rest.

His confidence has clearly taken a battering, and his latest international mistake has only increased the pressure.

Let’s be fair, young Herrick can’t perform any worse than the Danish keeper has in the last few games.

And as our recent coverage of supporters’ goalkeeping preferences demonstrated, there is already considerable dissatisfaction with the current situation.

I appreciate throwing a youngster into such an important game carries risks, but there comes a point when continuing with an out-of-form goalkeeper becomes an equally significant gamble.

For me, Saturday presents an opportunity to try something different.

Paul Mitchell could now emerge as a leading contender for a return to football after previously being considered by INEOS.

The Argentine, who has signed a contract until June 2029, is said to have made his concerns about Wilcox clear during discussions with the club hierarchy before accepting the managerial position.

Wilcox has come under scrutiny following United's disappointing recent form and questions over the quality and depth of the squad assembled during his time at the club.

Pochettino is keen to work with someone he trusts, having previously enjoyed productive spells alongside Mitchell at Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Mitchell was reportedly considered by INEOS for a senior football position in October 2023, before Wilcox ultimately took the role in April 2024.

Marcus Rashford's situation is one example of the wider challenge of moving players who no longer fit the club's plans.

Mitchell would bring considerable recruitment experience and, crucially, an existing relationship with Pochettino.

INEOS should not make a change simply to satisfy a new manager, but if Wilcox has failed to provide the squad-building structure and recruitment strategy United need, replacing him could be a sensible step.

Pochettino needs a sporting director who shares his vision, and Mitchell could be a compelling candidate to help deliver that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has provided an interesting insight into how West Ham United’s recruitment operation is working under Scott Parker, revealing that Nils Koppen is in regular contact with the coaching staff about the players the club needs.

Speaking in an interview with West Ham’s official website, Noble explained that the Director of Player Recruitment is arriving at Rush Green as early as 6.30am, watching training and discussing the squad with Parker and his coaches.

In a recent development, with the January transfer window approaching and West Ham desperate to secure promotion, it’s encouraging to hear that recruitment discussions are taking place. But for me, the most notable part of Noble’s revelation has very little to do with what time Koppen arrives for work.

Quite frankly, whether Koppen arrives at half six in the morning is neither here nor there.

Much of the analytical and recruitment work can be carried out perfectly well from wherever somebody can plug into the internet.

What I find far more vital is the open dialogue Noble has described.

He explained that Koppen watches training and that the coaching staff speak openly with him about the players they believe West Ham need.

Koppen then works with the club’s scouts and analysts in the background, allowing Parker and Noble to concentrate on coaching.

That strikes me as a huge plus and potentially a massive step in the right direction.

It also appears to represent a departure from the way things have operated previously, when questions were regularly raised about whether recruitment decisions matched the manager’s requirements.

As we discussed following Parker’s talkSPORT interview, the manager is absolutely right to concentrate on improving the players already at his disposal rather than becoming consumed by January transfers.

But that only works if the recruitment department understands precisely what he needs.

We know from our recent dialogue with a club insider that Koppen has begun looking for another striker, and Noble’s comments suggest those discussions are taking place alongside the coaching staff’s assessment of the squad.

That’s exactly how it should work.

Ultimately, I’m far more interested in whether Koppen signs the right players than whether he’s the first person through the door at Rush Green.

But if the people coaching the team and those recruiting for it are finally speaking openly about what West Ham need, that has to be encouraging.

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 07:20.

Union Berlin are in the midst of their second-worst start to a Bundesliga season, and things are not about to get any easier as the relegation contenders prepare to host an in-form RB Leipzig side this Saturday afternoon.

While Die Eisernen are languishing in the bottom three, Die Roten Bullen are eyeing up a fourth straight league victory as they continue to chase the Bundesliga’s top two.

With just seven points to their name from their opening nine Bundesliga matches, Union Berlin are already feeling the pressure.

Head coach Mauro Lustrinelli survived the international break, with the club's hierarchy seemingly prepared to give the Swiss tactician more time to turn things around.

However, his long-term future remains far from certain, particularly after director Horst Heldt cast doubt over whether the 47-year-old would still be in charge over the next five months.

Heldt also revealed that Union are already drawing up plans for the January transfer window, although with more than a month to go before it opens, any potential reinforcements are unlikely to provide Lustrinelli with immediate relief.

What may help the Swiss coach is the fact Union’s best results this season have come at home, with 86% of all their points coming at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Nevertheless, Union's defensive problems overshadow any slight positives, given they have already conceded 21 goals - a upcoming club record at this stage of a Bundesliga campaign.

While Union struggle to keep the ball out of the net, RB Leipzig simply cannot stop scoring at the moment.

Martin Demichelis and his men have already rattled the net 27 times in the Bundesliga this season - a total only bettered by Bayern Munich, who have scored on 29 occasions.

Just before the international break, Leipzig put five goals past Augsburg in a 5-2 victory - a game which extended their winning run to three straight league matches.

In recent times, Leipzig have also seen an upswing in their away results, winning their last two competitive games on the road - including a 2-0 success against Schalke at the end of October.

Striking early has been the key for Die Rotten Bullen so far this season, with the club yet to drop a point when scoring first in the Bundesliga.

In fact, the only major concern ahead of Saturday’s game is the fact Leipzig have lost four of their last six trips to Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Union Berlin form (all competitions):.

RB Leipzig form (all competitions):.

French defender Stanley Nsoki has missed every game this season for Union Berlin due to a muscle injury, and the 27-year-old will remain on the sidelines this weekend.

Robert Skov has only played one competitive minute this term, though he has recently returned to individual training.

Youngster Andrik Markgraf also remains out of action due to a knee injury, while Janik Haberer could miss Saturday’s game through illness.

When it comes to RB Leipzig, the visitors are also dealing with a handful of injuries as we head towards the end of the calendar year.

German midfielder Assan Ouedraogo has been out of action since September with a shoulder problem.

Youngsters Viggo Gebel and Marc Guiu are also dealing with knee and hamstring injuries.

Max Finkgrafe, meanwhile, has missed his last five games with a thigh injury, but is on the brink of a return.

Antonio Nusa, who has 11 goal contributions in nine Bundesliga games this season, is the man to watch for the visitors.

Union Berlin possible starting lineup:.

Ronnow; Juranovic, Van den Bosch, Friedrich, Rothe; Imeri, Schafer, Khedira, Aebischer; Ilic, Burke.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has now been reported that Newcastle United are interested in signing Kenneth Taylor in January.

The next transfer window is only six weeks away from opening.

Kenneth Taylor has proved a bargain buy by Lazio.

He was signed by the Serie A club in the January 2026 transfer window for a reported £15m plus future add-ons and in the second half of the 2025-26 season scored three goals and got two assists in 17 league appearances.

The left footed central midfielder has now played every league game so far this season and been a key factor in Lazio surprisingly topping Serie A at the moment, Kenneth Taylor adding two league goals and one assist so far this campaign.

The Netherlands international now a target for Newcastle United according to Tuttosport in Italy, with both Brentford and Bournemouth also credited with interest.

Lazio desperate to hold on to their star midfielder, rather than cash in and double their money in 12 months, with a valuation now of around £40m on Kenneth Taylor.

Sources indicate that kenneth Taylor was a teammate of Sean Steur’s at Ajax and won player of the year for the 2024-25 season when with the Amsterdam club. Taylor made 37 starts in the Dutch domestic league and Europa League, scoring 14 goals and getting seven assists. A bit of a surprise really that clubs in the Premier League and beyond didn’t show more interest in signing him in summer 2025.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham return to action tomorrow with a home tie against visitors Preston North End – a team who sit rock bottom of the Championship but are not without their recent triumphs after turning over promotion-chasing Southampton just before the break. So West Ham need to be wary, despite their opponents’ lowly league table position.

With Scott Parker having enjoyed an unbroken two week training period during the break, West Ham fans will now surely get to see the ‘Parker XI’ rather than Nuno’s inherited lin-up with which he began the first two games of his West Ham tenure.

The first visible difference will surely be to see -shock, horror – players used in their correct positions: Nuno because infamous for using square pegs in round holes – Morato at left back being the case in point.

Morata’s days at left back are surely over.

Despite being signed as a centre back and having played all but 33 of his last 177 games as such, Nuno insisted on using the 6’3 Brazilian – hardily the most mobile – as a left back who was frequently found to be out of position, often allowing wingers to get the better of him: Scott Parker hooked him at half time after a pretty inept left-back performance against Cardiff.

According to recent reports, with centre back Maximilian Kilman suspended for tomorrow’s clash there should be no more Morato at left back – incredibly West Ham fans have never seen the loanee in his preferred specialist position until now. Ezra Mayers has already done enough to start at left back leaving Parker free to slot Morato into the role for which he was signed, alongside Mavropanos.

It has been revealed that square pegs into square holes: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in his West Ham reboot. Who’d have thought.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Nations League draw has been made on Friday for England and the other seven League A teams.

England’s stunning win away to Spain meant that they won their group.

That meant they would be drawn against one of the teams who had finished runners-up in their group.

The Friday draw seeing England draw Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals.

It will be a two-legged tie in late March 2027, with Norway hosting the first leg, then England the benefit of home advantage in the second and deciding leg.

Then if they get through that, England will face either Belgium or Germany in the Nations League semi-finals in June 2027.

Fair to say that England have got what appears to be the easier half of the draw, as the four nations that they could play in the final are Netherlands, Portugal, Spain or France. Spain v France obviously looking the pick of the quarter-final ties.

I have seen some in the media claiming a Nations League victory would end 61 years of hurt with a first major tournament win since 1966.

It would be great for England to win it but nobody is seeing this surely on any kind of similar level to the Euros and World Cup.

At best I think you could see the Nations League on a similar level as the Conference League at club level, with then Euros and Europa League also compared to each other, as well as World Cup and Champions League, when comparing national sides and club ones when they play in the various competitions.

#26576. Industry News: The question for Saudi Arabia PIF: Is this a staging post at Newcastle United, or the destination?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: The question for Saudi Arabia PIF: Is this a staging post at Newcastle United, or the destination?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Saudi Arabia PIF led takeover came with PSR headroom from the Mike Ashley years and looser rules on owner-linked sponsorship.
  • Around £450m went on transfers in the Amanda Staveley era, but it was spent steadily, not decisively, and commercial income never grew fast enough to fund the next step.
  • By June 2024 Yankuba Minteh and Elliot Anderson had to go for a combined £60m-plus just to stay inside PSR.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Saudi Arabia PIF led takeover came with PSR headroom from the Mike Ashley years and looser rules on owner-linked sponsorship.

Around £450m went on transfers in the Amanda Staveley era, but it was spent steadily, not decisively, and commercial income never grew fast enough to fund the next step.

By June 2024 Yankuba Minteh and Elliot Anderson had to go for a combined £60m-plus just to stay inside PSR.

The structure never worked. Amanda Staveley was bought out in July 2024. Dan Ashworth left for Manchester United.

Paul Mitchell lasted under a year, branded the transfer operation “not fit for purpose” and ended up in a turf war with Eddie Howe which was largely irrelevant as every financial decision was made by Saudi Arabia PIF. Mitchell might have identified the problem but he had no answers.

Sources indicate that darren Eales and Dan Ashworth struggled to get past PIF’s processes. Good football people kept failing inside this framework. At some point you have to blame the framework.

It has been revealed that I agree Eddie Howe came back much too early and fatigued mentally and physically. But he still delivered the Champions League football.

Recent findings suggest that last seasons 12th with 17 league defeats was a bitter pill swallow and faced with the fresh strategy and sale of his best players he walked away in July. He certainly was not at his best and was working with a divided squad where both Gordon and Tonali indicated to the club they were leaving before Christmas.

The central concern is our senior players simply had much higher earning potential at the six clubs who do not face the same SCR restrictions. Alexander Isak was reportedly assured of an improved deal by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi in March 2024. Paul Mitchell shelved it and Eddie Howe publicly cited PSR as the reason. Isak downed tools. Every dressing room and every agent drew the same conclusion: PSR then, SCR now, this club can’t pay you what you’re worth. So Gordon, Tonali and Bruno followed him out, with Trippier also gone.

Sources indicate that blaming Eddie Howe for transfers is a simplistic and nuanced view. None of the players signed in summer 2025 were his first choice, the embarrassing prolonged struggle to get transfers over the line are a clear manifestation of that. Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were signed two weeks after the season started in desperation. That after the board took direct control of the Alexander Isak situation and prevented Eddie Howe from communicating with the player.

Recent findings suggest that beware the convenient narrative. It was Amanda Staveley’s naivety, then Paul Mitchell’s manner, then Alexander Isak’s greed, then Eddie Howe’s stubbornness. Now it is Matthias Jaissle’s tactics or Ross Wilson’s signings. A new scapegoat every season is very useful to the people who never change. When the same problems outlast every individual blamed for them, the individuals were never the problem.

Under Ross Wilson the newly introduced model has seen eight of the summer’s signings being 24 or younger, including 18-year-old Sean Steur from Ajax for about £20m. Dortmund is the stated template. Roughly £249m of players went out. The CEO’s line is that anyone under contract leaves “on our terms.”.

The problem is they still leave. Call it what it is: develop to sell. Under SCR, trading profit inflates the revenue side of the ratio, so I understand the logic.

Newcastle United are mid-table under Matthias Jaissle with the youngest squad in years. The question for Saudi Arabia PIF: is this a staging post at Newcastle United, or the destination?

#26574. Xabi Alonso's January transfer proposal dealt cruel blow as Chelsea 'barred' from signing £30m maestro

📖 Baca

Xabi Alonso's January transfer proposal dealt cruel blow as Chelsea 'barred' from signing £30m maestro

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (407 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:31, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:32.
  • Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.
  • The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:31, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:32.

Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.

The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Juventus are determined to keep hold of the highly-rated winger, with a potential departure at the moment considered off the table.

Alajbegovic was pursued by Chelsea during the summer after impressing at RB Salzburg, but the west London club's proposed project failed to convince the youngster.

The Blues were understood to be considering sending him out on loan rather than offering immediate first-team opportunities, allowing the Serie A giants to secure his signature instead.

There has now been renewed interest from Alonso's side, but reports in Italy (via Sport Witness) suggest Chelsea face an uphill battle to bring the 19-year-old maestro to Stamford Bridge.

It is claimed that Alajbegovic 'isn't leaving' Juventus, with the Italian side pleased by his development and unwilling to consider an exit despite interest from England.

The £30m teenager is also happy with his role in Turin, where he believes he has the right environment to continue developing, with similar reports suggesting that he wants to remain at Juventus for a 'long time'.

As a result, an immediate departure has been described as 'truly barred', making a January transfer particularly difficult to negotiate.

Chelsea's interest is understandable given the Bosnian's potential, but the club may struggle to convince him that Stamford Bridge is the right place for his development.

Regular first-team football should be a priority for a teenager at this stage of his career, and Juventus are right now providing him with opportunities to establish himself.

By contrast, Chelsea's sizeable squad creates greater competition for attacking positions, with even highly-rated youngster Estevao having experienced his own difficulties securing consistent game time.

That situation could serve as a warning to Alajbegovic, particularly when he is already enjoying an increasingly prominent role in Turin.

Although Juventus may not offer the most stable environment, they are giving the youngster opportunities to develop at senior level.

Chelsea might be able to offer a lucrative project, but unless they can guarantee a clearer pathway into the first team, Alajbegovic would arguably be better off remaining in Italy.

Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

📅 03 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher.
  • It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together.
  • Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Sources indicate that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian stated. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Sources indicate that still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

Sources indicate that this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he noted he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

Industry observers note that it is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9.

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw.

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:.

It has been revealed that “Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”.

Lewis Hamilton indicates this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

According to recent reports, “I love this energy [from the crowd]. Substantial, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA.

According to recent reports, “It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”.

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he noted he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Recent findings suggest that excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

It has been revealed that hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL.

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

In a recent development, the other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Recent findings suggest that russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Recent findings suggest that hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Sources indicate that russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one latest set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls).

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv.

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

Sources indicate that 11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin).

Mercedes have put a brand fresh set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

It has been revealed that antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a significant moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

It has been revealed that how about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen presently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

In a recent development, that has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he states Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It has been revealed that it’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

Industry observers note that he added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

Sources indicate that the two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

Recent findings suggest that what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Recent findings suggest that most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Sources indicate that bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

Sources indicate that the two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

Industry observers note that the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Recent findings suggest that not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change rapidly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be notable to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara presently leads the Formula 2 championship.

Sources indicate that TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

It has been revealed that aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who remarked the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti remarked. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really vital that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

According to recent reports, “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

Industry observers note that with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Sources indicate that formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Sources indicate that verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a latest floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a 'surprise' move for Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap as Roberto De Zerbi looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The 23-year-old has revived his career at the City Ground following a difficult spell at Chelsea, attracting renewed interest from north London.

However, a potential deal could be more complicated than initially expected, with Forest placing a substantial valuation on their summer signing.

According to FootballTransfers, Delap is 'admired' by De Zerbi, with Spurs continuing to monitor the former Ipswich Town forward after tracking him during the summer transfer window.

Delap has scored three goals in his first nine Premier League appearances for Forest, offering encouraging signs following his disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge.

A January move is considered extremely difficult, though, given Forest only signed him in the summer and are unlikely to sanction his departure while fighting for their Premier League status.

Tricky Trees owner Evangelos Marinakis is not expected to approve a mid-season sale, although it is understood that De Zerbi could be prepared to wait until the summer of 2027.

Forest are likely to demand around £75m for the Englishman, which would represent a significant profit on the initial £45m they paid Chelsea.

There is no denying that Delap has shown some improvement at Forest, but his overall Premier League goalscoring record remains a significant concern amid Spurs' renewed interest.

His three goals this season take his career total to just 16 efforts in 76 Premier League outings, while he managed only three goals in 47 appearances for Chelsea.

Those numbers hardly suggest a striker capable of immediately resolving Tottenham's attacking problems, particularly if Forest demand £75m to part with him.

Spurs still need a reliable source of goals if they are to climb the table and compete for major honours, rather than another expensive gamble on potential.

De Zerbi's admiration is understandable, but Tottenham should be wary of paying a premium for a forward whose top-flight returns remain underwhelming.

Delap may yet develop into an excellent striker, but spending that much on him would represent a considerable risk for a club with more pressing needs.

West Ham’s Home Advantage Problem Won’t Disappear With 60,000 Fans

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.
  • Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.
  • It has been revealed that he also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

It has been revealed that he also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s crucial to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that it was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

And our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

The news that Turkish Superlig side Trabzonspor are interested in one of West Ham’s squad would not normally be welcomed with unbridled enthusiasm, particularly in January when there’s such a short window to bring in replacement players.

However when the report confirms that the Turkish title contenders are focussed on Pablo Felipe there’ll probably be universal approbation amongst supporters who have had to sit and endure – though gritted teeth – the Portuguese forward’s West Ham career fail to ignite.

One solitary league and one cup goal is the extent of his output which, for the 20 million plus that was inexplicably paid, is not nearly good enough. Almost, but not even, Niclas Fullkrug – like performance.

One Claret and Hugh reader labelled him ‘The striker that cannot shoot, head, trap or pass the ball’ : He has always looked like one with the demeanour of a spectator plucked from obscurity as a competition winner to represent the team he came to watch, rather than a €20 million signing.

“The world loves a trier” – West Ham fans would prefer a goal scorer.

So the news that there’s a side actually lining up a bid for the forward this winter can only be seen as a good thing for the club and probably for Pablo himself.

As Turkish site fanatik confirms:.

Which will add fuel to the fire of speculation that the Irons are indeed planning on a new striker acquisition this winter: Sadly, there’s no way the money spent on Pablo or for that matter the £27 million blown on Taty Castellanos will be fully recouped.

The hope can only be that with Nils Koppen running transfers this winer there may be slightly more productive arrivals.

In a recent development, unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times.

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :.

According to recent reports, “Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

In a recent development, “And I love that. As you said, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz).

The pressure will be significantly eased with a clean sheet and three points tomorrow – whether Soucek now, 31 gets into the action or simply acts as a calming figure in the dressing room. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 08:09.

Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga will come from the Veltins Arena in Gelsenkirchen, as Schalke 04 welcome Stuttgart for a tasty league encounter.

The hosts have endured a dreadful start to the season and are still looking to score their first home goal, while the visitors are setting their sights on a third successive league success.

Schalke ended their five-match goalless run last time out against Hoffenheim, although their attacking breakthrough counted for little as they suffered a 2-1 defeat.

That result left Die Konigsblauen sitting in the relegation zone during the international break, while head coach Miron Muslic avoided an early sack.

Nevertheless, the 44-year-old remains under considerable pressure, with Schalke now enduring a seven-game winless streak across all competitions.

Even more concerning for the Royal Blues faithful is the fact that their points tally after nine Bundesliga matches is identical to the one they recorded at the same stage of their disastrous 2022-23 campaign, which ended in relegation.

In order to turn things around, the hosts will need to start scoring goals, otherwise they risk becoming just the second team in Bundesliga history to go without a goal across their first five home matches of a season.

There is one positive for the hosts and that is the fact they beat Stuttgart when these two teams last met back in February 2023 - their only victory over the Swabians in five previous meetings.

While Schalke are on the ropes, Stuttgart are on the attack, with the Swabians looking to record their third straight Bundesliga win.

Sebastian Hoeness and his side powered to a 1-0 win over Werder Bremen just before the international break, leaving them just six points adrift of the top four.

Given their sluggish start to the campaign, Stuttgart's recent upturn represents a welcome change in fortunes, with their defensive improvements playing a significant role.

Two clean sheets from their last three domestic outings make for much better reading than the two shutouts they managed across their opening 10 matches of the season.

Stuttgart will now turn their attention to landing their first league win over Schalke since 2021 - the only success over the Royal Blues they boast in 12 previous meetings.

What’s more, the Swabians have not managed to win at the Veltins Arena since 2013 - losing four and drawing three of their last seven trips to Gelsenkirchen.

Schalke 04 form (all competitions):.

Stuttgart form (all competitions):.

Along with their goalscoring problems, Schalke are also dealing with a lengthy injury list.

Maximilian Wober and youngster Luca Vozar are both currently out with hamstring injuries.

Defender Timo Becker picked up a foot problem just before the international break, and will also remain on the sidelines.

Emil Hojlund is yet to feature for Schalke this season due to an Achilles injury, while midfielder Ron Schallenberg is out with a leg problem.

Stuttgart are also missing a handful of names, including midfielder Angelo Stiller who is struggling with an adductor injury.

Swiss defender Luca Jaquez featured in the 1-0 win over Bremen before the international break, but he has since become a doubt due to a ribs problem.

Youngsters Jarzinho Malanga and Justin Diehl complete the injury list, with the two players carrying thigh and abdominal issues.

Meanwhile, forward Deniz Undav missed out on selection for the German national team, with the 30-year-old still looking for his first Bundesliga goal this season.

Schalke 04 possible starting lineup:.

Karius; Ayhan, Katic, Kurucay, V. Becker; El-Faouzi, Tanaka; Ljubicic, Karaman, Aouchiche; Hwang.

Stuttgart possible starting lineup:.

Seimen; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; El Khannouss, Undav; Demirovic.

Schalke are simply not scoring at home, and they could struggle here against an improving Stuttgart defence.

The visitors have struggled away in Gelsenkirchen over the years, but this is the perfect opportunity to improve that record.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 18:36 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:37 EST, 16 November 2026.

Max Dowman broke another record as the 16-year-old became the youngest-ever goalscorer for England's Under-21 side on Monday night.

The Arsenal teenager has already broken a plethora of records at club level, and is now taking that to the international stage too, breaking a record set by senior team star Jude Bellingham, who scored aged 17 years and 67 days in 2020.

Dowman was called into the U21 squad for the first time this international break, and made his debut off the bench in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal on Friday.

On Monday, meanwhile, he was given a start by manager Lee Carsley, and rewarded his manager's faith with an 89th-minute winner to break the record and earn his side a 3-2 win.

It's a record he can add to his already-extensive collection, which includes being the youngest Champions League player, the youngest Premier League goalscorer, and the youngest Premier League winner.

Industry observers note that manager Lee Carsley said after the game: 'He played really well - he was one of four or five outstanding performances. Mikey Moore, Max, Ethan (Nwaneri), they were very good.

Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goal scorer when he scored against France on Monday.

Industry observers note that 'We see how good on the ball he is but he was outstanding off the ball. You have to keep reminding yourself about his age. There's a lot of expectation around him and he seems to handle that so well.

Sources indicate that 'It's key we keep supporting him and he develops at his own pace. It's so important he enjoys his football.

'Obviously all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can.'.

Despite bursting onto the scene last season, Dowman has just 19 minutes to his name in the top flight this campaign as Arsenal look to defend their title.

He has played a number of games for the Gunners' U21 side, while he was sent off against League Two side Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup.

Arteta scolded his player at the time, but said: 'I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. Whether that's positive or negative. You need to understand the context, the relationship I have with him and what we discussed before we went out.

'If you see the reaction from my mother and father with me sometimes, you'd say "you don't like that reaction", but for me it was the best reaction ever as it enabled me to be who I am.

The Arsenal teenager, 16, broke the record held by Jude Bellingham with his late winner.

Industry observers note that 'But you want to see the best and most beautiful reaction. You want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with 10 men.

According to recent reports, 'What do you expect? That's the level and that's the reaction. Whether it's right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, I'm f****d off, massive time.

Sources indicate that 'This is the environment and the reality. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much but we are also demanding as he needs to earn the right to play otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me?'.

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:12.

Bruno Fernandes will be bidding to inspire Manchester United to a huge victory when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

The match will mark Mauricio Pochettino's first fixture in charge of the 20-time English champions, and he will be hoping for inspiration from his captain.

Fernandes has found it difficult to show his best form for the Red Devils this season, but the 32-year-old has still managed to come up with six goals and three assists in 14 appearances.

Here, Sports Mole looks at how the Portugal international has performed against Liverpool during his professional career.

Fernandes has faced Liverpool on 13 previous occasions during his professional career, boasting a record of five wins, three draws and five defeats.

The attacker has scored three times against the Reds, in addition to contributing two assists.

Eleven of Fernandes' appearances against Liverpool have come in the Premier League, boasting a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats, scoring twice and registering two assists.

Fernandes has also faced Liverpool twice in the FA Cup, helping Man United to record a 3-2 win in the fourth round of the competition in 2021, finding the back of the net, before playing in a 4-3 success for the Red Devils in the quarter-finals in March 2024.

The Portuguese's two Premier League goals against Liverpool have been at Old Trafford, so he would create some personal history by finding the back of the net at Anfield on Sunday.

Last season, Fernandes provided an assist in a 2-1 Man United win at Anfield, before helping the Red Devils record a 3-2 victory in the reverse game at Old Trafford.
